A 13-seed mean of about 0.7534 is roughly 0.34 pp above the official bar, which is a comfortable margin there. H4 mixes the two up: it treats 'true mean near 0.753' as a risk for the judge, when the real problem is local. Any change re-draws seeds 0-2, so the usable budget for time cuts is about +0.04 pp, not the 0.31 pp E069 appears to give.
critiques.suggestion: Split H4 into two claims: (a) official safety, now supported by the 13-seed data, and (b) regression to the mean against the local gate. Under (b), only changes that are accuracy-neutral or better in expectation can be stacked. Margin recovery should come before any further time cut.

With benchmarking, the chosen conv algorithm can differ between processes, and with it the floating-point reduction order. An identical commit may then no longer give bit-identical accuracy. Nobody has rerun an unchanged commit since. E028's 0.003 pp match hints at determinism, but it could equally be a no-op edit.

If per-group lr multipliers were not applied in the compiled path, then E039 (head x0.5, wd x2) and E045 (head x2, wd x0.5) were really wd-only changes, and so were the BN-lr runs E056 and E072. The simpler reading is that the slope is still about 1.4 pp/epoch (0.70 pp over 0.5 epoch, consistent with the earlier 1.14) and both points carry ±0.2 pp of noise. They were also measured on different bases (E061 freeze-0.7 vs E069 PE). H6 still says the marginal epoch is worth only about 0.3 pp, H6.4 is 'open' and H6.4.1 is 'open' with E070-.

critiques.target: E076 surprise (eval-mode BN in frozen block 1: -0.54 pp)
critiques.issue: The notebook writes this off as noise against an optimistic draw. Still, -0.54 pp is the largest of the 'neutral' children. With block 1 frozen, switching its BN to running stats should, if anything, make training match eval. A real loss of this size would suggest either a bug (buffer handling in the compiled eval-mode graph, or lookahead blending of buffers) or that block 2 relies on batch-stat noise. The verdict was given on time alone; the accuracy mechanism was never examined.
critiques.suggestion: Check whether all three seeds dropped by a similar amount, and compare final BN buffers with E069's. If the drop is consistent, record it as evidence about H7.2, the block-2 noise dependence. Do not close it as noise.

critiques.issue: Under Muon, block-1 and block-2 widths (128/384), the whitening patch size and width, residual connections, and Muon momentum below 0.6 were never varied. Only block-3 width and block-1 depth were tested. H6.1.2 (18 px) is the cheap test of the 1x1-map explanation for E050 and was not run. No Lvl1 hypothesis covers architecture shape beyond H1.5 and H5.
critiques.suggestion: Add a node for reallocating width between blocks 1 and 2 at matched FLOPs. E037 suggests Muon uses capacity efficiently. Run H6.1.2 offline if it is cheap.

critiques.target: What the Lvl1 set fails to explain
critiques.issue: No Lvl1 explains why noise estimates keep rising: about 0.06 pp (E057), 0.14 (E070), about 0.24 (E075). It also does not explain why the E069 base gives such large losses for small edits, or why identical changes cost different amounts on different bases (block-1 freeze at 0.7: -0.11 on E058, -0.38 on E069). Each is handled with an ad hoc per-run story ('cost grows with whitening', 'convex knee').
critiques.suggestion: Add a Lvl1 or H4 mechanism: noise on the 3-seed mean depends on the base and grows as the recipe moves closer to the knee and to stronger whitening. Test it with RNG-shift controls on E058 and E069, and re-rate keeps under 0.25 pp against that measured noise.

That is roughly 0.27 pp below its seeds-0-2 score, so the PE 'win' (H1.2.7, a single 3-seed run) may be mostly a lucky draw. It also explains why all seven children of E069 lost 0.1-0.9 pp: regression to the mean against an inflated baseline. Several 'refuted' verdicts (E073, E074, E076) are therefore weaker than recorded.

On the actual objective, the fixed seeds 0-2 at >= 0.753, the real budget for time cuts is about 0.04 pp, not 0.31. Only math-preserving cuts are safe until margin is rebuilt: Gram NS, projection frequency, and re-checking autotune for the PCIe judge. The 13-seed data already shows comfortable official safety (about 0.75 + 0.34 pp), which H4 does not acknowledge.

Two foundations need re-checking. First, H4.1.1's determinism evidence predates cudnn.benchmark and max-autotune. Second, H1.6.6, the no-op check rated highest priority, was never run, yet the closures of the head-lr, BN-lr and lookahead axes depend on it. E070 refutes H6.4 and the 'marginal epoch is worth 0.3 pp' claim; the asymmetric-knee story is ad hoc, and a slope of about 1.1-1.4 pp/epoch plus noise fits both runs. Many statuses are stale (H1.2.4, H6.3.1, H6.4.1, H7.1.1, H7.2.1, H7.3.1, H1.11.1, H1.7.4).

Margin-recovery directions never tried: Muon lr 0.20 on the PE base, the averaging ramp and sync interval, and width reallocation between blocks 1 and 2. No Lvl1 hypothesis explains why noise estimates keep rising (0.06 → 0.14 → 0.24 pp) or why identical changes cost different amounts on different bases. The next step is RNG-shift controls on both E058 and E069.
